original_title: Clayface Trailer Teases Other Batman Villains
summary_en: DC Studios unveils a chilling teaser for their upcoming horror film, 'Clayface,' showcasing the villain's terrifying transformation. The trailer hints at a darker Gotham, featuring familiar landmarks and a potential lineup of iconic antagonists.

en.title: Clayface Trailer Drops Gruesome Glimpses of Gotham's Rot
en.summary: DC Studios unveils a chilling teaser for their upcoming horror film, 'Clayface,' showcasing the villain's terrifying transformation. The trailer hints at a darker Gotham, featuring familiar landmarks and a potential lineup of iconic antagonists.
en.body:
Gotham City is no stranger to darkness, but the upcoming **Clayface** film, directed by **James Watkins**, is set to plumb new depths of terror. The official teaser trailer has just dropped, and it’s a visceral plunge into the grotesque metamorphosis of Matt Hagen, portrayed by **Tom Rhys Harries**. This isn't your typical superhero fare; it's DC Studios' first official dive into the horror genre, and the trailer leans heavily into its unsettling tone.

The narrative centers on Hagen, an aspiring actor whose life takes a horrifying turn after a mobster disfigures his face. Desperate, he tests an experimental serum, a decision that unleashes a monstrous transformation. The trailer doesn't shy away from the body horror, presenting Hagen's struggle to maintain his physical form in a series of disturbing, melting sequences. We see the sheer agony of his flesh deforming, a truly nightmarish visual that promises a raw and unflinching portrayal of the character.

## Unearthing Gotham's Underbelly

Beyond Hagen's personal descent into monstrousness, the trailer offers tantalizing glimpses of a wider Gotham underworld. We're introduced to **Naomi Ackie** as the enigmatic mad scientist Caitlyn Corr and **Max Minghella** as a hard-boiled Gotham detective, suggesting a complex web of characters entangled in Hagen's fate. Crucially, the trailer features a prominent Gotham landmark: Club Vesuvius. This minor, yet significant, venue in Batman comics history is depicted as a seedy establishment frequented by the rich and famous. The trailer hints that this club has become a hideout for villains like Firefly, and that the notorious Black Mask may have acquired it, setting the stage for turf wars and escalating chaos.

## A Rogues' Gallery Revealed?

The inclusion of Club Vesuvius and the implied presence of **Firefly** and **Black Mask** strongly suggest that **Clayface** won't be a solitary affair. While the focus remains squarely on Hagen's tragic and terrifying arc, these Easter eggs signal a broader narrative that connects to the wider tapestry of Batman's infamous rogues' gallery. The trailer builds to a particularly grim set piece involving Hagen's oozing eyelids, emphasizing the extreme measures he'll take to cope with his condition. It’s a bold statement from DC Studios, signaling a willingness to explore its characters through a more mature and frightening lens, potentially setting a new standard for superhero horror.

## What's Next

**Clayface** is slated for release in theaters this October. With its emphasis on psychological horror and grotesque transformations, fans can anticipate a truly unique and unsettling cinematic experience from the DC universe.

tr.title: Kil Yüz Trailer'i Gotham'ın Çürümesini Gösteriyor
tr.summary: DC Studios, yakında çıkacak olan 'Kil Yüz' filmi için ürpertici bir fragman yayınladı. Fragman, kötünün dönüşümünü gösteren Gotham'ın karanlık bir dünyasını sunuyor.
tr.body:
Gotham City karanlığa alışık bir şehir, ancak **James Watkins** tarafından yönetilen yakında çıkacak olan **Kil Yüz** filmi, terörün yeni derinliklerine dalacak. Resmi fragman yayınlandı ve **Tom Rhys Harries**'in canlandırdığı Matt Hagen'in iğrenç dönüşümüne bir dalış yapıyor. Bu, tipik bir süper kahraman filmi değil; DC Studios'un ilk resmi korku filmi ve fragman, rahatsız edici tonuna ağır basıyor.

## Gotham'ın Alt Dünyasını Keşfetmek

Hagen'in kişisel olarak canavarlığa dönüşümünün ötesinde, fragman daha geniş bir Gotham alt dünyasına dair büyüleyici bakışlar sunuyor. **Naomi Ackie**'nin oynadığı gizemli deli bilim insanı Caitlyn Corr ve **Max Minghella**'nın canlandırdığı sert bir Gotham dedektifi ile tanışıyoruz, bu da Hagen'in kaderine karışan karmaşık bir karakter ağı olduğunu gösteriyor. Önemli olarak, fragman, Batman comiclerinde önemli bir yer olan Club Vesuvius'u gösteriyor. Bu, zengin ve ünlü insanların ziyaret ettiği bir mekan olarak betimlenen kulüp, Firefly ve Black Mask gibi kötülerin sığınağı haline gelmiş gibi görünüyor, bu da toprak savaşları ve artan kaosu tetikleyebilir.

## Bir Suçlu Galerisi Mi?

Club Vesuvius'un dahil edilmesi ve **Firefly** ile **Black Mask**'in varlığının ima edilmesi, **Kil Yüz**'ün yalnız bir iş olmayacağını güçlü bir şekilde öneriyor. Hagen'in trajik ve korkunç yoluna odaklanılırken, bu Easter egg'ler, Batman'ın infamous suçlu galerisine bağlanan daha geniş bir anlatıyı işaret ediyor. Fragman, Hagen'in akışkan göz kapaklarına dair特别 bir set parçasıyla doruğa ulaşıyor, bu da durumuna uyum sağlamak için alacağı aşırı önlemleri vurguluyor. DC Studios'tan cesur bir açıklama, karakterlerini daha olgun ve korkutucu bir lens aracılığıyla keşfetmeye istekli olduğunu gösteriyor, potansiyel olarak süper kahraman korku türünde yeni bir standart belirliyor.

## Sonraki Adım

**Kil Yüz**, Ekim ayında sinemalarda gösterime girecek. Psikolojik korku ve iğrenç dönüşümlerine odaklanmasıyla, hayranlar DC evreninden真正 olarak benzersiz ve rahatsız edici bir sinema deneyimini bekleyebilir.

content_raw: While we’re all a little disappointed that Matt Reeves has pushed The Batman: Part II back to 2028, and we’re all annoyed that we still have no details on an official DCU Batman , that doesn’t mean we have to stay out of Gotham City. The upcoming film Clayface will bring the shapeshifting villain to the screen before the Dark Knight, telling the story of up-and-coming actor Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries) who tests an experimental serum after a mobster mangles his face. The latest trailer for Clayface helps us get over the lack of Batman by leaning hard into its horror tone. Not only do we meet Naomi Ackie as mad scientist Caitlyn Corr and Max Minghella as a Gotham City detective, but we get to see Hagen struggling to keep his melting flesh together. The trailer even builds to a stomach-churning set piece in which Hagen takes extreme measures to deal with his oozing eyelids. But in between all the gross body stuff, one might catch a glimpse of an important Gotham landmark, one that involves baddies Black Mask and Firefly. Throughout the trailer, Hagen visits Club Vesuvius, a minor venue used in Batman comics and other media. For the most part, the Vesuvius serves as a s rich and famous. Along the way, they encounter Firefly, a minor villain who had been hiding out in the abandoned club. Across the arc, we learn Black Mask acquired Vesuvius at some point and has given it to Firefly in exchange for his services. However, Firefly has his own agenda and sets large swaths of the city on fire in retaliation for all that’s gone wrong in his life. Black Mask confronts Firefly at Vesuvius, and the two attempt to kill one another until Batman and Robin arrive to stop them. As the above description indicates, Vesuvius is hardly one of Gotham’s most important landmarks, in the same way that Firefly is hardly a top-level villain. While Black Mask did appear in Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn) , played by Ewan McGregor , Firefly has yet to show up on the big screen. That’s because Warner Bros. Discovery canceled the 2022 Batgirl movie to get a tax write-off, despite the fact that it featured Brendan Fraser as Firefly. So why include Club Vesuvius in Clayface? The answer is more simple than you’d think. Clayface writer Mike Flanagan has cited as inspiration the Batman: The Animated Series entry “Feat of Clay,” and the trailer’s shots of a mangled Matt Hagen recall the character design from that classic two-parter. Batman: The Animated Series was primarily developed by Bruce Timm, Mitch Brian, and Paul Dini, the guy who wrote Streets of Gotham . The inclusion of Club Vesuvius is likely a nod to Dini’s work and, in particular, his love of Zatanna. But it might also be a way to sneak Black Mask and Firefly into the new DCU.
